newsitem.title: OMAN: GULF'S FIRST FATTY ACID PLANT PLANNED IN OMAN.
newsitem.headline: GULF'S FIRST FATTY ACID PLANT PLANNED IN OMAN.

text.p: Omani and foreign investors plan to set up the Gulf's first fatty acid plant in northern Oman producing raw materials for the soap, detergent and pharmaceutical industries, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Oman Daily Observer said the 3.5 million ($9.3 million) project was being promoted by Keemya Oman, set up to make and sell chemical products from the Sohar industrial estate north of the capital Muscat.

The paper quoted V. Sundaresan, general manager of The National Detergent Co -- which will hold 12.5 percent of the new company -- as saying it would offer 40 percent of its shares to the public later this year.

The plant plans to make products used in the manufacture of household and industrial cleaners, coatings, adhesives and fabric softners from vegetable oils like palm oil, palm kernel oil and coconut oil, sourced mainly from Malaysia and Indonesia.

Other major investors in the venture were named as Bhacker Suleiman Jaffer, with 12.5 percent, the Omzest group with 10 percent, Oman International Development and Investment Co with 8.5 percent and Detraco with seven percent.
